company.name: Tallybridge
company.description: Expense management for mid-size companies: employees pay, finance teams approve, and every payment lands in the ledger.

title: Tallybridge: month-end is coming
brief: Tallybridge closed its Series A on a promise of moving upmarket. Sales is bringing larger prospects with long lists of demands, support is drowning ahead of month-end, and the engineering manager warns the platform is getting fragile. You have one sprint before the busiest week of the month. Decide what the team commits to.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 32 tickets, 8 are traps and 2 critical problems are filed as minor. Mid-sprint, losing an engineer forces a replan: the plan that wins keeps room to react.
hidden.principle: One customer is an anecdote, five are a pattern. Build for the pattern and negotiate with the anecdote.

stakeholders.name: Carmen
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Yuki
priorities: Close the deals in this quarter's pipeline
Never tell a prospect 'it is not on the roadmap'

stakeholders.name: Andrés
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Rafael
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Irene
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

stakeholders.name: Jonas
priorities: Customer money and data handled by the book

tickets.title: TLS certificate for the API expires in 9 days
tickets.description: Automatic renewal broke after the DNS move. When the certificate expires, every integration and the mobile clients stop connecting.

visible.impactHint: Hard date: expires in 9 days.

hidden.explanation: A total outage with a known date and a tiny fix. It is in the sprint before anything else is discussed.

tickets.title: Hold and send balances in EUR and GBP
tickets.description: Customers with European suppliers convert through their bank and lose on the rate. They ask whether we will support other currencies.

visible.impactHint: Asked for by 14 accounts this quarter.

hidden.explanation: Real demand from several accounts, but it needs new banking partners and licences. Too big to justify against cheaper wins this sprint.

tickets.title: Fix the flaky test suite
tickets.description: One in three CI runs fails for no reason and is simply re-run. Engineers estimate half a day lost per person every week.

visible.impactHint: Roughly 10% of engineering time is lost to re-runs.

hidden.explanation: It moves no product metric, yet it hands back capacity in every future sprint. It pays for itself within two.

tickets.title: Guided setup checklist for new accounts
tickets.description: New accounts land on an empty home screen. Session recordings show most of them leave before completing the first key action. A four-step checklist would walk them to it.

visible.impactHint: Funnel data: 58% of signups never finish setup.

hidden.explanation: The biggest leak in the funnel is at setup and it hits every new account. Few tickets move activation this directly, and the claim comes with funnel data.

tickets.title: Replace 'Something went wrong' with actionable errors
tickets.description: Every failure shows the same generic message. Users cannot tell whether to retry, fix their input or contact us.

hidden.explanation: Reduces confusion and some tickets, but it spreads thin across many small cases.

tickets.title: Let customers invest their idle balance
tickets.description: Everyone I talk to wants their balance to earn something. We should offer an investment product.

visible.impactHint: Everyone I talk to wants this.

hidden.explanation: 'Everyone I talk to' is a sample of the CEO's network. A new regulated product needs demand data first, and none exists.

tickets.title: Bulk edit and bulk delete in list views
tickets.description: Power users clean up their data one row at a time. Some send support a spreadsheet and ask us to do it for them.

hidden.explanation: Saves real time for the heaviest users and removes a recurring support task.

tickets.title: Native tablet app
tickets.description: I am sure a lot of our users would love us on a tablet. A founder friend with a similar product says tablets are huge for them.

visible.impactHint: A founder friend says tablets are huge for them.

hidden.explanation: A hunch and one anecdote. Nobody has checked how much traffic comes from tablets; that check takes an afternoon and comes before a 13-point build.

tickets.title: Activity log for account admins
tickets.description: Admins want to see who changed what and when. Security questionnaires from larger prospects ask for it explicitly.

visible.impactHint: Currently blocking two security reviews.

hidden.explanation: A genuine requirement for larger accounts, but it only matters to a slice of the pipeline and it is not small.

tickets.title: We find out about outages from customers
tickets.description: Support learns that something is down when tickets pile up, then tells engineering. The system should warn engineering first.

visible.impactHint: Three incidents this quarter were reported by customers.

hidden.explanation: Same work as TAL-289 ("Alerting on error rates and queue depth"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Header briefly shows a stale account name after deploys
tickets.description: After the last two deploys, two users reported that the header showed another company's name for a moment. A refresh fixed it. Probably a caching quirk.

hidden.explanation: One customer seeing another customer's data is a cross-account leak, not a cosmetic glitch. If the cache mixes names it can mix anything.

tickets.title: Show the estimated arrival time of payouts
tickets.description: After sending money, users see 'Processing' with no date. Many write to ask when it will arrive.

hidden.explanation: Cuts a common question with very little work. Modest but efficient.

tickets.title: Sign in with Google
tickets.description: Signup requires creating a password and confirming an email. A one-click option would remove two steps from the top of the funnel.

hidden.explanation: Removes real friction at signup, though the size of the lift is an estimate.

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Retry after a timeout sometimes sends the transfer twice
tickets.description: Seen three times last month when the bank API was slow. Operations reversed the extra transfers manually.

visible.impactHint: Seen 3 times last month.

hidden.explanation: Sending a customer's money twice is the worst thing a payments product can do. Three cases at today's volume become dozens when the bank has a bad day.

tickets.title: Board dashboard with weekly KPIs
tickets.description: The CEO assembles the board numbers by hand from three tools every month. A dashboard would give them live.

hidden.explanation: Saves one person a couple of hours a month. Real but small, and no customer ever sees it.

tickets.title: Monthly statements as PDF
tickets.description: Accountants need an official statement at every month end. Today support generates each one by hand on request.

visible.impactHint: Statement requests spike to 300+ tickets at month end.

hidden.explanation: Removes the single largest batch of manual support work and gives customers something they need every month.

tickets.title: SAML single sign-on for larger accounts
tickets.description: Security teams at larger prospects will not approve a tool without SSO. Sales has been answering 'soon' for two quarters.

visible.impactHint: Required in 6 open deals; 3 were lost over it last quarter.

hidden.explanation: The same requirement across many deals is the market talking, not one customer. Expensive, but it unlocks a whole segment.

tickets.title: Search: typo tolerance and recent items
tickets.description: Search only matches exact words. One in five queries returns nothing, and most of those are misspellings of things that exist.

visible.impactHint: 21% of searches return zero results.

hidden.explanation: A real, measured friction for regular users. Solid mid-value work, though not cheap.

tickets.title: Fix contrast and keyboard focus on the core flows
tickets.description: Fourteen screens fail WCAG AA contrast and the main form cannot be completed with a keyboard.

visible.impactHint: Fails WCAG AA on 14 screens.

hidden.explanation: The right thing to do and a growing requirement in procurement, but no deadline is attached yet.

tickets.title: Cut deploy time from 50 minutes to 10
tickets.description: A deploy blocks the pipeline for almost an hour, so fixes are batched and hotfixes are slow.

visible.impactHint: The team deploys twice a week instead of daily.

hidden.explanation: Speeds up every release and every hotfix. Good value, but not a small job.

tickets.title: Custom PDF report layout for Halvorsen Group
tickets.description: Halvorsen Group wants our reports in their corporate template, with their logo, fonts and a signature block. Their procurement team calls it a condition for renewal.

visible.impactHint: Halvorsen Group is our third largest account.

hidden.explanation: One customer's template, hard-coded into the product. Nobody else has asked. The 'condition' is a negotiating position: a paid services engagement or a plain export covers it.

tickets.title: Search and filters in transaction history
tickets.description: History is one long list by date. Finding a payment from last quarter means scrolling, so users ask support to look it up.

hidden.explanation: A daily annoyance for active accounts and a steady source of tickets. Solid mid-value work.

tickets.title: Help links in the app point to deleted articles
tickets.description: After the help centre migration, eleven in-app links lead to a 404 page.

hidden.explanation: Small value, but almost free. A good filler when one point is left.

tickets.title: Home screen takes 6 to 9 seconds to load for large accounts
tickets.description: The home query loads every record before paginating. The accounts with the most data, which are also the ones that pay the most, get the slowest product.

visible.impactHint: p95 load time is 8.4s for the top 10% of accounts.

hidden.explanation: Performance pain concentrated in the highest-value accounts, backed by measurements. It protects retention where it matters most.

tickets.title: White-label the product for Pinnacle Freight
tickets.description: Pinnacle Freight wants to resell us under their own name and domain, with our branding removed everywhere including emails.

visible.impactHint: Pinnacle Freight says they could bring 40 clients.

hidden.explanation: A new business model decided by one partner's promise. 'Could bring' is not a signed commitment, and the branding work touches every surface.

tickets.title: Show remaining daily and monthly limits
tickets.description: Users discover their limit when a payment is refused. The remaining amount is not shown anywhere.

hidden.explanation: Prevents a predictable failure and the ticket that follows. Small, tidy win.

tickets.title: Apply the new brand colours across the whole app
tickets.description: The rebrand launched on the website last month. The app still uses the old palette on about 60 screens.

visible.impactHint: Users see two different brands.

hidden.explanation: Everyone sees it and nobody behaves differently because of it. It can ride along with other UI work over time.

tickets.title: Cut the signup form from nine fields to three
tickets.description: Six of the fields are never used after signup. The variant with three fields has already been tested.

visible.impactHint: A/B test last quarter: +11% completed signups.

hidden.explanation: Already validated by an experiment and nearly free to ship. The best value-per-point ticket in most backlogs.

tickets.title: Downloadable account statements for bookkeeping
tickets.description: Prospects with an external accountant ask whether they can download official statements themselves. Right now the answer is 'email us'.

hidden.explanation: Same work as TAL-296 ("Monthly statements as PDF"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Rewrite the pricing page before the price change
tickets.description: New prices go live on the 1st. The current page still describes the old plans and would show wrong numbers at checkout.

visible.impactHint: The new prices go live either way.

hidden.explanation: Not every CEO request is a trap. This one has a fixed date and a concrete cost if it slips: customers shown the wrong price.

tickets.title: Shareable 'Your year in money' cards
tickets.description: An animated year-end summary users can post on social media, like the music apps do. Great for brand awareness.

visible.impactHint: Great for brand awareness.

hidden.explanation: People share music taste, not business payment totals. Reach on paper, no path to any metric that matters.

midSprintEvents.title: Marta is out for the rest of the sprint
midSprintEvents.description: Marta, one of the senior engineers, is on unexpected leave from today. Their work in progress has to be picked up by the rest of the team.

hidden.guidance: Capacity dropped, so scope has to drop with it. Cut the lowest-value work and protect the critical tickets. Asking the team to absorb the difference is how sprints fail quietly.
